record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: Polish 1/2-CDH spaces without dense open CDH subspaces
record.original_question: Does there exist a Polish space that is 1/2-CDH, meaning that it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms, and that has no dense open countable dense homogeneous subspace?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Is there a 1 2 -CDH Polish space without a dense open CDH subspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space X is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets D, E of X there exists a self-homeomorphism h of X such that h(D) = E. More generally, for a cardinal κ, X is called κ-CDH if the action of the self-homeomorphism group of X on the family of countable dense subsets of X has exactly κ orbits; thus a 1-CDH space is precisely a CDH space, and a 2-CDH space (written here as "1/2-CDH" in the sense of having exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms) is one in which there are exactly two such orbits. Recall that a Polish space is a separable, completely metrizable topological space.

Question: Does there exist a Polish space X that is 1/2-CDH (i.e., has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under the action of its self-homeomorphism group) and such that X has no dense open subspace that is countable dense homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the literature on countable dense homogeneity. Recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 arXiv preprints on CDH spaces and powers of Polish spaces) continue to investigate n-CDH variants without indicating that this particular question has been resolved. No published resolution was located.
